concept.name: Close-only order
concept.definition: An order instruction restricting the order to closing (fully exiting or reducing) an open position, so that execution can never establish or add to a position. On derivatives platforms it appears both as a standalone close-position function and as a 'close on trigger' flag on conditional orders.
concept.intuition: Close-only means the order's only job is to get you out - it cannot turn into a new bet in the opposite direction.
concept.mechanics: The platform ties the order to the open position: quantity is bounded by the position size, and if the position no longer exists when the order triggers or arrives, the order is rejected or canceled. Close-on-trigger variants attach this behavior to stop/take-profit orders so a late trigger cannot open a reverse position.
concept.failure_modes: A close-only order submitted after the position has already been closed is simply canceled, which can leave a hedge or paired leg unexpectedly live. During liquidation or margin stress the venue may prioritize, resize, or cancel closing orders in ways the trader did not anticipate.
concept.misconceptions: Close-only is often treated as identical to reduce-only; in practice close-only usually targets full position exit (and is rejected with no position), while reduce-only strictly bounds any execution to position-reducing size. Neither guarantees execution price.
concept.example: Short 5 ETH contracts, you place a close-only buy stop; when the trigger fires it buys back at most the 5 contracts needed to flatten, and if you already covered manually, the order is refused rather than opening a long.
